title: Trump eases Canada tariffs ahead of US midterms
summary: The move comes as Trump's Republican Party scrambles to maintain control of the US Congress, with a Republican candidate in a key Senate race saying she had lobbied to lift the tariffs on Canadian…

image.caption: Trump had slapped some Canadian goods with a 50% tariff in the summerImage: Janelle Dumalaon/DW

blocks.text: US President Donald Trump has lifted some of the tariffs imposed on Canada amid an economic row with the US' neighbor to the north, which peaked this summer.
The White House on Friday said the easing of tariffs will apply to products including "plywood sheets, some paper products, certain machinery and refrigeration equipment."
The changes will take effect on October 30.
US-Canada trade war: The cost of fighting back
What do we know about the Canada tariffs relief?
The White House said the president was seeking to offset "the burden to US commerce while better serving the public interest.''
The move comes less than two weeks ahead of the November midterm elections, where Republican candidate Susan Collins is locked in a tight race with Democratic challenger Troy Jackson in Maine.

Collins said on Friday she'd addressed the tariffs with Trump's top trade negotiator, Jamieson Greer, and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, adding that she raised with the due the issue of "the toll tariffs are taking on Maine families, businesses, farmers, and growers.''

"Many of our farmers and growers rely on specialized equipment, packaging materials, and other products from Canada that are either unavailable from American suppliers or cannot be replaced without incurring significant expense," Collins said.
She added that she had asked for tariff relief and vowed to "encourage a broader trade agreement with Canada, our neighbor, ally, and largest trading partner."
While the latest move reliefs some of the tariffs, it also imposes new levies on goods including carpets, certain valves and waste products, the White House said.
